content_summary: Our whole codebase defers annotations and anything generic falls over at conversion time with a TypeError about the parametrized form. Non-generic models are fine, so we pin the old release for now.
Every whole-converter policy can be set once except the one we actually need, keying on aliases. We restate it per model and someone always forgets one.
Annotating a field as a read-only collection does not stop us getting a mutable one back, so our models are unhashable and callers mutate them. Mostly a documentation surprise, but it bites.
We run conversion in a worker pool. Errors coming back over the process boundary cannot be rebuilt, and the extra-keys message reshuffles its field names every run so our log dedup is useless.
A plain JSON number gets rejected by a field typed as float even though the pass-through set includes both numeric types. Every type checker disagrees with that.
The subclass registry is great until the hierarchy is generic or uses mixins, then registering it just raises an AttributeError. Nice library otherwise.
Our enums carry tuples as member values and nothing round-trips - the payload still holds live enum objects and reading it back raises. Plain string enums are fine.
Would love to describe per-field serialization next to the field instead of in a separate registered hook. Right now adding a field silently changes the payload shape.
